item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Trump Plans to ‘Blockade’ Strait He Insisted Must Open
item.summary: The president’s threat came after Saturday’s talks failed to produce a deal for peace or the full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Both sides suggested further negotiations were possible.

item.title: In Pakistan Talks, Iran Saw a U.S. Trying to Dictate, Not Negotiate
item.summary: Iran sees American demands as reaching far beyond what the United States achieved in war. Tehran is gambling that it can withstand further bombardment more than Washington is willing to sustain economic chaos, experts say.

item.title: Inside Tyre, a Lebanese City Bombarded by Israel
item.summary: In Tyre, a city on Lebanon’s coast, near-daily bombardments by Israel have killed and injured civilians, and left many searching for shelter.

item.title: Iran’s Underground Air Force Base Was Hit Earlier in the War
item.summary: Satellite imagery shows impact craters at and near the tunnel entrances to aircraft shelters at Iran’s remote “Eagle 44” base.

item.title: Cuba’s President Projects Defiance in Standoff With the U.S.
item.summary: Miguel Díaz-Canel’s stance on “Meet the Press” reflected how Cuba is digging in against pressure from a Trump administration distracted by the war in Iran.

item.title: Israel Launches New Attacks in Lebanon, Days Ahead of Rare Direct Talks
item.summary: Israel’s campaign targeting Hezbollah in Lebanon has been a source of tension in the U.S.-Iran cease-fire. Israeli and Lebanese officials plan to meet for rare talks in Washington this week.

item.title: The ‘Islamabad Peace Talks’ Are Over. What Now for Pakistan?
item.summary: With the U.S. and Iranian delegations gone from Islamabad and the cease-fire uncertain, Pakistan faces its own economic and diplomatic challenges.

item.title: Rejected by Dozens of Emergency Rooms: South Korea’s Medical Crisis
item.summary: Hundreds of patients every year have trouble finding emergency care, even though the country has a world-class medical system. For some, the delays have been fatal.

item.title: Mass Stampede at Haitian Tourist Site Leaves Dozens Dead
item.summary: The tragedy unfolded around the appearance of a social media personality at the Citadelle Laferrière, a fortress that is a symbol of Haitian sovereignty.

item.title: Jailed for Love Songs? Yes, and Still Singing.
item.summary: Nguyen Van Loc was persecuted for performing Hanoi’s old romantic music during (and after) the Vietnam War. He can’t stop. He won’t stop.
